sources.claim: Traffic allocation is revision-specific; tags expose a revision URL even with no allocation from the main service URL. Traffic changes have a transition period, so the fixture supplies later completed snapshots.

Service trafficStatuses reports routing state; reconciling, terminalCondition and observedGeneration distinguish completed reconciliation from desired traffic. generation and observedGeneration use string JSON representations.

Cloud Run request records and cloud_run_revision resource labels support revision-scoped investigation. The packet's cohort summaries and synthetic application error text are authored observations, not provider guarantees.

a.conclusion: The monitored service-URL regression follows serving revision 00032-mnw after the completed 14:00 traffic change, against the observed healthy 00031-akt baseline. Newest 00033-jqr is not the failing serving revision. The exact 4.8.0 defect is still unproven.
next_checks: Application owner compares 4.8.0's preview calculation/configuration with 4.7.1 using the failing request IDs.
Release owner checks current readiness, dependency compatibility and capacity of 00031-akt as the evidence-backed rollback candidate before seeking approval for a bounded traffic change.
Morgan checks current service-URL user outcomes through the existing TLC; the historical baseline alone does not prove recovery.
unsupported: Blame newest 00033-jqr solely because it is newest.
Treat all failures as tagged-only or infer healthy main-service traffic.
Declare a rollback executed, safe without current checks, or sustained recovery achieved.
Declare the exact code defect or total customer impact from the limited cohort.
unknowns: Current capacity/compatibility of 00031 and post-window outcomes.

b.conclusion: The newest revision 00033-jqr has zero main-service allocation but receives failing trial-tag URL requests. The sampled main service URL continues successfully on 00031-akt. This packet does not support a main-service rollback or a claim that zero allocation means zero requests.
next_checks: Release/test owner identifies the callers and intended use of the trial-tag URL and investigates 4.8.1 before promotion.
Morgan separates tag and main-service cohorts in the incident update and asks the authorized logs reader for the broader user-impact window.
Keep traffic decisions with the release owner; current 00031 observations support retaining its allocation while investigating the tag.
unsupported: Blame a main-service rollout to 00033 or recommend rollback as if it were serving the main URL.
Dismiss the 12 failures because the revision has zero allocation.
Label tag requests non-customer test traffic without caller evidence.
Declare universal health or recovery from the sampled service-URL cohort.
unknowns: Who uses the tagged URL and their business impact.
Exact cause of the 4.8.1 calculation error.
